title: Employee Rights
summary: Employees are entitled to fair wages, safe working conditions, non-discrimination, and lawful termination procedures. These rights are protected under constitutional and labour laws.
next_steps: Keep employment records, appointment letters, and salary slips.
Raise the issue with the employer or HR department first.
Approach the Labour Department or Labour Court if the grievance is not resolved.
official_source: Constitution of India and labour statutes

title: Salary Payment Rules
summary: Employers must pay wages on time and cannot make unauthorized deductions. Delayed or unpaid wages can be challenged before the appropriate labour authority.
next_steps: Gather salary slips, bank statements, and appointment documents.
Request a written explanation from the employer.
File a complaint with the Labour Department if wages remain unpaid.

title: Complaint Procedure for Employment Grievances
summary: Workers can file complaints for unpaid wages, wrongful termination, unsafe conditions, or unlawful deductions through labour authorities and courts.
next_steps: Maintain all supporting documents and written communications.
File the complaint at the appropriate Labour Office or labour court.
Seek legal aid if the matter is complex or the employer is unresponsive.

title: Right to Equality
summary: Every citizen is equal before the law. No person can be discriminated against based on religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
next_steps: Report discrimination to the appropriate authority.
Seek legal assistance if your rights are violated.

title: Right to Education
summary: Children between the ages of 6 and 14 have the right to free and compulsory education under the Constitution and the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009.
next_steps: Contact the local school or education department.
File a complaint if admission or education rights are denied.
Approach the District Education Officer if the issue is not resolved.
official_source: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009

title: Right to Information (RTI)
summary: Citizens have the right to seek information from public authorities, except where the law exempts disclosure on grounds of privacy, security, or public interest.
next_steps: Submit an RTI application to the relevant public authority.
Mention the specific information sought clearly.
Appeal to the appropriate appellate authority if the request is denied.

title: Free Legal Aid
summary: Persons who are poor, marginalized, or otherwise unable to afford legal representation may receive free legal aid through legal services authorities.
next_steps: Contact the nearest Legal Services Authority.
Provide identity proof and basic case details.
Request legal assistance for court matters or pre-litigation advice.
official_authority: NALSA / State Legal Services Authority / District Legal Services Authority

title: Consumer Rights
summary: Consumers can seek remedies for defective goods, deficient services, unfair trade practices, or misleading advertisements. The law provides for refunds, replacement, repair, or compensation.
next_steps: Keep bills, warranty cards, and communication records.
Contact the seller or service provider first.
File a complaint with the appropriate consumer forum if the issue remains unresolved.

title: Right to File an FIR
summary: Any person who has knowledge of a cognizable offence may approach the police to file an FIR. The police must register the complaint and investigate the matter.
next_steps: Go to the nearest police station or use the emergency helpline.
Provide all relevant facts and supporting evidence.
Follow up with the investigating officer if the matter is not acted upon.

title: Women's Rights
summary: Women have the right to dignity, equal protection, safety, and freedom from gender-based violence. Special laws also protect them against workplace harassment (POSH) and domestic abuse.
next_steps: Seek immediate help from local authorities or a shelter if you are in danger.
Document evidence of abuse or harassment.
Approach the police, women’s commission, or legal aid services.
official_source: Constitution of India, POSH Act, Domestic Violence Act

title: Senior Citizen Rights
summary: Senior citizens are entitled to financial and social protection, including maintenance support from children/heirs and protection from neglect or abuse.
next_steps: Report neglect or abuse to the local Maintenance Tribunal or Social Welfare officer.
Keep documents proving maintenance, kinship, or property rights.
Seek help from the legal services authority if needed.
official_authority: Maintenance Tribunal / Courts / Social Welfare Department
official_source: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007

title: Child Rights & Safety
summary: Children have rights to protection, education, healthcare, and a safe environment. Their welfare is protected by constitutional, child-labour, and child-protection laws like POCSO.
next_steps: Report abuse, neglect, or exploitation to child protection authorities.
Contact the local Child Welfare Committee (CWC) or police.
Seek legal aid if the child’s rights are violated.
official_authority: Child Welfare Committee / Police / Juvenile Courts
official_source: Constitution of India, Child Labour Act, POCSO Act 2012

title: Rights of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)
summary: Persons with disabilities are entitled to equal opportunity, accessibility, non-discrimination, and support services under the law.
next_steps: File a complaint if accessibility or equal opportunity is denied.
Approach the Disability Commissioner or relevant local authority.
Seek legal aid or assistance from support organizations.
official_source: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016

title: Refund Rules for Defective Goods
summary: Consumers can seek a refund, replacement, repair, or compensation if a product is defective, not as described, or a service is deficient.
next_steps: Keep the bill, warranty card, and product details safe.
Contact the seller or service provider first in writing.
File a formal complaint through the Consumer Commission or online grievance portal if they refuse to remedy.
official_authority: National Consumer Helpline / Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission

title: Consumer Helpline 1915
summary: The national consumer helpline number 1915 is a government-supported channel for consumer grievances, complaints, and guidance. It connects consumers to relevant authorities.
next_steps: Call 1915 for initial guidance on your complaint.
Provide product/service details, purchase information, and issue description.
Keep the complaint reference number safe for future follow-up.
official_source: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Government of India

title: Cybercrime - Online Fraud & UPI Scams
summary: Fraudulent digital transactions, phishing attacks, SIM swap fraud, or fake payment confirmations are serious criminal offences punishable under BNS 2023.
next_steps: Block your credit cards or bank accounts immediately.
Report the transaction details to your bank within 24-72 hours to invoke zero-liability.
File a complaint at the national cybercrime portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or call the Cyber Helpline 1930.
official_authority: National Cybercrime Cell / Cyber Police Station

title: Workplace Sexual Harassment (POSH)
summary: Every woman has the right to a safe working environment free from sexual harassment. Employers must form an Internal Committee (IC) to address such complaints.
next_steps: Submit a written complaint to the Internal Committee (IC) or Local Committee (LC) within 3 months of the incident.
Request conciliation or immediate interim relief like transfer or paid leave for up to 3 months.
If the employer fails to act, report to the District Officer or file a police report.
official_source: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act, 2013

title: Traffic Laws - Motor Vehicles Act
summary: Governs the licensing of drivers, registration of motor vehicles, traffic regulation, third-party insurance, and penalties for violations like drunk driving (minimum 6 months disqualification).
next_steps: Always carry valid digital/physical copies of your driving licence, registration (RC), pollution certificate (PUC), and insurance.
Under Section 185, drunk driving leads to immediate vehicle impounding and court fines/disqualification.
